reviews.text: Dr. De Bonis knows everything and is spot on. I call him the clinic's wizard. He's truly professional, and all the staff are friendly and kind. Highly recommended.

...alas, I thought I had found a welcoming and excellent center...and instead I found an affordable center...in a few days I brought Polpetta...operated for two stupid things...for them...in a few days my beloved cat...still had problems...brought back...to this center...Polpetta never came home...because after further tests...she had serious oncological problems...that they hadn't detected in the first appointment...??...I can't believe it...they were making fun of me...how disgusting...
Efficiency, professionalism and above all great empathy, thank you from the bottom of my heart.
Optimal

What can I say? My dachshund has been treated with care and love by Dr. Vincenzo for years. He was just a few months old, now he's almost 19 years old, a great achievement! Thank you for the love, accuracy, and professionalism you always show, and for the precision, scrupulousness, and finesse. Great love and passion. Thank you for always knowing and for taking care of Eolino all these years!
Thank you for your positive feedback! Pet welfare and owner satisfaction are our top priorities.

Cookie and I found the people professional and very helpful.
Thank you!
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.
Super kind, welcoming and prepared doctors.
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.

I thank Dr. Magagnini and his entire staff for taking on the situation of an Abruzzese Shepherd with a severe dislocation. The dog was fostered at a shelter and arrived in terrible condition. The dislocation had been present for several months. Dr. Magagnini was the only surgeon who agreed to examine the dog and intervene where possible. The dog is now doing well, with only a limp that allows him to live a nearly normal life, a condition that would have worsened with any other alternative. Dr. Magagni is one of those veterinarians you can trust.
I brought the dog for the annual vaccination, the phone says one price, the payment says another
Thanks to all the staff for caring for and saving my little girl!!!!!
Well done, they saved our beloved guinea pig, careful and scrupulous👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼👏🏼 …
Mamma mia, to be avoided

I'm giving two stars, not one, because the doctor who took my cat's x-ray was very kind, but the night before I called to ask about the cost of the x-ray. They told me it was about 70 euros, 130 x-rays, two taken but not requested! What if I hadn't had the money? See, you said 70 the night before?
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!
I would like to give a positive review regarding the welcome, competence and empathy demonstrated by Dr. Krushova.
Thank you for your review! Our team works hard every day to provide the best service possible.
We are happy to know that our efforts are appreciated and that you had a positive experience with us.
Your kind words truly make us happy! Our team works hard every day to provide attentive and professional service. Knowing that you appreciate our work is the best reward. Thank you for your trust!
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!

Professional and helpful, I took my cat to an emergency clinic with a urinary blockage, which he was admitted to and then operated on by them. They treated me with compassion and expertise.
I go to them all the time now, and I can't recommend them enough!

TERRIBLE!! DO NOT BRING YOUR PETS HERE!!!
They brought a dog with a cough, and they were fine. After a few days, the dog died.

The doctors are highly trained and kind. We used their top-notch night service. They are affiliated with the Gregorio VII Veterinary Clinic.
NB: The Prenestina clinic's 24-hour emergency service will no longer be available starting April 1, 2026. However, it will remain open during the following hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00 AM to 8:00 PM.
Dr. Giuseppe and Dr. Ludovica are extremely attentive, kind, and knowledgeable!

Highly recommended for anyone who loves caring for their pets.
Qualified and loving staff.
Precise and helpful.

I already knew this veterinary clinic, and today I was delighted to return because Dr. Magagnini, the veterinarian I've always trusted, has been working here for some time.

We had routine tests done on my dog, and the results were delivered the same day, which I really appreciated. The clinic is spacious, clean, and welcoming, and the staff was very kind and helpful.

Dr. Magagnini is always a guarantee: professional, attentive, and very caring with animals. My dog ​​trusts only him, and that says it all for me.

Highly recommended.

Highly recommended clinic! We brought our dog for melanoma, and Dr. Magagnini was very humane and professional throughout the process, from diagnosis to post-op, performing the operation flawlessly. Nerina had no problems during or after the operation, even though she's a 12-year-old dog. Many thanks to Dr. Magagnini and the entire clinic staff!

I took my dog ​​for an abdominal ultrasound, and we had a great time. The clinic is very well-maintained and attentive to the animals' needs. The doctor who performed the ultrasound was extremely kind, knowledgeable, and thorough in his explanations.
Dr. Magagnini, who has been treating our dog for years, is a guarantee of professionalism, expertise, and love for animals, as always! Highly recommended clinic.

I arrived one night because my dog ​​had fallen off the couch, and I wanted to make sure he hadn't broken his leg, since he was limping a bit. The doctor on duty didn't even examine him; he immediately took X-rays, which weren't necessary; all it took was a touch and he would have immediately known nothing was broken. The worst part is that the price list for the services isn't posted anywhere. In the end, he presented me with a bill for €245. He even expressed disappointment, saying he hadn't charged me for one of the X-rays. In reality, that X-ray had been poorly done by him because it was missing a piece he'd forgotten to add. Of course, he wouldn't have charged me for it! I'm furious. I go to work and no one gives me money for free. Not informing the client in advance of the costs involved doesn't seem to be very legal!
Punctual and very professional visit, my little Maltese had a bad gastroenteritis, treated excellently!
It's an excellent veterinary clinic, excellent doctors and surgeons, kind and good staff and I've been going there for a while and they're all good, especially Dr. De Bonis.
We're so happy to read your review! Our team works passionately to offer the best for every pet. Thank you for sharing your experience!

I took my dachshund for an orthopedic appointment and had a wonderful experience.
Dr. Manuel Magagnini was truly sweet, attentive, and highly competent.
The puppy was calm and happy from the start, and even during the blood draw, the doctor was extremely gentle, calm, and able to instill peace of mind, both for me and the dog.
You can immediately sense his passion and respect for animals. He's a professional who puts you at ease and works with great humanity.
I highly recommend him.
Thank you for your positive feedback! Pet welfare and owner satisfaction are our top priorities.

I can only speak badly of this clinic. I took my dog ​​to have a simple cyst lanced, and they recommended not to use general anesthesia. Instead, that evening when I went to pick her up, they had done it. The next day she died. It would have been right to report them.

It doesn't even deserve one star, but I'm forced to give it one.

A terrible experience in every way: lack of empathy, zero emotional support, minimal explanations, and a cold and annoyed attitude toward customers concerned about their pets.
Excellent service, correct diagnosis, rapid intervention
A disaster

Stay away from these incompetent people. Their only goal is to extract as much money from you as possible by making vague diagnoses, selling you their medications, and performing superficial examinations of your pets. Avoid them like the plague.

DON'T EVEN BRING A MOUSE
Our dog had a stomach upset (a critical situation for a dog) and was taken in by this guy late at night only AFTER he had done another dog, which clearly wasn't urgent. I'd like to point out that the person at the facility had been notified an hour in advance by phone. Furthermore, the thing that made my blood boil the most, and caused us to waste even more time, was the fact that, instead of offering first aid as a matter of priority, he started asking for our information and so on, when he could have done it later.
There was no option to pay in installments for the operation, which is shocking in my opinion.
The only positive note: the guy recommended another clinic.

I took my dog ​​to the aforementioned veterinary clinic recommended by an acquaintance who praised it so much, but from the start he didn't trust me. I had an appointment at 4:30 pm and the visit started at 6:00 pm, unaware of who would examine my dog ​​who was suffering from presumed lymphoma. I must say that the dog was walking and was lively at that point they drew lots among the three doctors who were there to examine the dog.... while coming in and out and minding his own business, the doctor immediately listed a series of tests, needle aspirations, ultrasounds and so on... I'll make a long story short, he put his hands on my dog ​​for a needle aspiration and immediately the dog showed he could no longer walk, he didn't eat me for three days, paralyzed on the sofa and when I asked for the results of the test they mocked me that they would send it by email, which they didn't do. I strongly advise you not to bring your dearest loves to that clinic, they are only there for profit and that's it, they don't care about the lives of animals.

I arrived at this clinic one evening around 9:30 PM to have my cat's paw treated because he had gotten into a fight with the other cat in the house at 8 PM and was injured. The closest Borghesiana clinic to us wasn't available due to an imminent transfer, so we opted for the emergency room at this other clinic. To make a long story short, I rang and no one came. I rang a second time and a nurse arrived, I think with a smile, I think a foreign accent. He didn't ask me any questions but I explained everything. He started by saying that the emergency room costs 105 euros, as if to clarify the situation. Well, I left without doing anything, first because they didn't inspire trust in me, and second because they didn't give me complete information. I took the cat to the clinic down the street the next day and they did everything that needed to be done calmly. No empathy, congratulations!

My experience with this facility was devastating. From the beginning, I received confusing and contradictory information. First, I was told that an X-ray could rule out lung metastases; based on this, I authorized the surgery to remove her uterus.

After the operation, my dog ​​began to feel terrible: she was breathing with difficulty, with her mouth open. The risks of the surgery were never clearly explained to me, nor what could happen in the days following. When I brought her back, despite having an appointment, I waited over an hour, while she was clearly in pain.

At that point, I was told that further tests were needed, such as a CT scan, because "perhaps" there were metastases. So before, the X-ray was enough, but after the surgery, it suddenly wasn't enough anymore.
I was also told that there was a lot of fluid mixed with blood in her lungs and that I would have to wait two days for a precise result. My dog ​​died before those results came back, and after her death I received no concrete explanation, only instructions on how to pay for her ashes and if I wanted to collect her.

The most painful moment was seeing her on oxygen: I was told to turn it on "a little," and I did exactly as instructed. She looked at me, howled, and died before my eyes.

Throughout this entire process, I felt unprotected, and I saw no protection for my dog.
I'll share what I experienced: a confusing, inconsistent, and, for me, deeply unacceptable handling of her situation.

Please: do your research before entrusting yourself to anyone. Don't make the same mistake I did.

A special thanks to Dr. Leci and Dr. Krushova for their compassion and their help until the end for my beloved Birillo.
Thank you for caring for my dog ​​during this fragile moment and accompanying him to the bridge as peacefully as possible.
Thank you so much ❤️

If I had known this was the case, I wouldn't have admitted my beloved cat Bilbo. I was forced to take him to the clinic's emergency room on October 10th for urgent tests and an abdominal ultrasound. It was assumed, as was later confirmed, that he was suffering from kidney failure. I was seen by Dr. De Bonis, who immediately after the tests and ultrasound told me that the case was serious and that I should leave him for four or five days to put him on an IV until his kidney parameters returned to normal. I followed his advice with hope, and so Bilbo was admitted, despite all the anguish of separation for me. The next day I went to visit him. He was in his cage with an Elizabethan collar, an absorbent mat, a bowl of kibble—which, as I had already said, he wouldn't eat because he had no teeth—and a water bowl without water. I had to fill the bowl myself to get him to drink. I left him so as not to interrupt his therapy until he had further tests. I always had to call to check on him, and the phone was always busy, or the doctors were busy, and I never got a call back. When I went to see him on Sunday, I was made to feel bad about going because there was only one vet in the emergency room and not even a nurse. I found him in appallingly unsanitary conditions, soaked in urine, with the litter box filled with urine and a single sheet of newspaper. The vet justified himself by saying he was alone, even though there were only three cats in the hospital; it wouldn't take much to clean. I agreed, however, that we'd call in the afternoon to see how he was doing. When I called the doctor, after much insistence, he told me he hadn't done his rounds yet! I can assume he hadn't even checked the IV. On Monday, I went for another visit and found Dr. Alvino, who would run the follow-up tests and let me know the results by midday. I was worried because Bilbo's future depended on those tests, but the doctor didn't call. In the afternoon, I called and the response to my complaints about not being called was, "Look, you could have called too." Absurd, especially since every time I called, either the doctor was busy or the secretary would tell me the doctors were busy. Unfortunately, the tests hadn't given the results I'd hoped for, and after four days of therapy, there was no hope. So on Tuesday, I brought him home, in a pitiful state, even hygienically, but he was revived as soon as he saw us arrive. He was discharged by another vet, who instead gave me a little hope. (Did he realize the situation?) At home, I only had to administer supplements according to them... All for the modest sum of €610! By Thursday, October 16th, he was too sick, and I had to take him to a veterinary practice I know to let him go.
It was a Via Crucis lived with great pain, and also with anger at having found people who didn't empathize with these poor little creatures, at least in my case. If I could do it again, I would keep him with me, having him undergo, as the vet told me, day hospital treatment and then take him home in the evening. It would have been less painful for us and especially for him. I'm sorry, but I don't recommend this clinic.

I found a very good orthopedic vet named De Bonis, and I still go to him. I highly recommend him, and he's also an ultrasound technician. I read some very negative reviews, but they've saved several colony cats for me, and De Bonis was very thorough and humane. Another cat was operated on by Felli, and everything went very well. Unfortunately, sometimes there are pathologies that leave no cure; this isn't the vets' fault.

Useless nighttime emergency room. I paid €105 for nothing, and for only having my dog's temperature checked and checked for symptoms.
My dog, after years, returned for urgent convenience, but I still hold the same opinion as years ago! A useless nighttime emergency room.

On August 30th, my 18-year-old cat started acting up, and my regular vet was closed. We were lucky enough to find this clinic, and Dr. Krushova in particular. He immediately identified the problem and prescribed a treatment that, after a week, proved highly effective! I highly recommend the entire clinic, and the doctor in particular, for his empathy and expertise!
Thanks to all the doctors for the professionalism with which you welcomed us and helped my dog ​​Asia

I brought my dog ​​with vomiting and diarrhea. The doctor had zero empathy, but hey, everyone has their own personality. The dog was in an emergency, but I still had to wait a while because there was only this doctor and there was a kitten before me. Finally, I went in for an ultrasound, and he first assumed she had a uterine infection. Then we moved on to x-rays, which ruled it out and diagnosed gastroenteritis. The dog had obviously lost fluids due to diarrhea and vomiting. He advised me to go to another clinic in Romanina for a specialized ultrasound. I got there, but the sonographer wasn't there. The dog died, and the cause was hypovolemic shock, meaning organ failure due to lack of fluids. This should be an emergency clinic, meaning they should provide the necessary treatment quickly. And that should have been to replace the fluids my dog ​​had lost. Not to send me to another clinic and waste any more of my precious time. He was honest about one thing, that the dog was at risk, and in fact she died!! But would she have died anyway if she'd immediately applied the necessary treatment instead of sending me here and there, given that you're an emergency clinic and emergency room? Maybe so, but the doubt certainly remains strong!

I didn't know about the clinic until the day my Sansone developed back pain. A friend recommended it, and I'm grateful for introducing me to this clinic. The environment is spotless, always in perfect order. The staff is extremely kind and knowledgeable.
Sansone had to undergo three surgeries at once to avoid having to sedate him three times. The surgeon, Dr. Felli, was excellent but above all human, giving me peace of mind and peace of mind. They even called me in the days after the surgery to find out. I recommend the facility because it's truly unique and humane, and I will always be grateful.
Thanks to the entire team.
After three months, I had to bring my Sansone back urgently at night because he was having an epileptic seizure. Dr. Stefano did everything he could to help stabilize him, and he was hospitalized for three days. Parting ways with him was hard, but I must say that I was always called and kept updated on how Sansone was responding to the treatment. They allowed me to see him during his hospitalization and to spend time with him. I will never stop thanking this facility and this team. Thank you from the bottom of my heart.
They are the real dogs and with this I limit myself to saying more
Clinic open 24/7, my ass, we waited outside for half an hour and rang the bell, no answer, we called no answer, luckily my dog ​​is not in danger of dying.

Two weeks later, I'm writing this review to strongly advise against Bluvet for **emergencies at night or on holidays**.

My cat, Diesel, suffering from struvite, was initially treated by a very competent doctor (Dr. Ervis Leci), whom I thank for his professionalism and honesty. However, the following evening, I found myself seeing another veterinarian, Dr. Vincenzo Alvino, who handled the situation in an **unfair and manipulative** manner.

He convinced me to admit him by leveraging the seriousness of the situation, my guilt, and my financial difficulties, **promising discounts and free services** (including an ultrasound), **which were never fulfilled**. He didn't even attempt to empty the cat's bladder, which was the real emergency and the reason I returned (I would have admitted him to my regular clinic the following morning). In the end, I paid around **€600 in three days**.

When I pointed out the inconsistencies and complained about the treatment I received, I was threatened with a slander lawsuit and reported as a problem client simply for not accepting admission immediately.

I also had an unpleasant experience with the receptionist, who made an offensive scene in front of other customers because the banknotes were slightly wet (due to a bottle of water in my bag).

🔴 I will never return to this facility. It's a real shame, because in the past I've had positive experiences with excellent doctors like Costanza and Giuseppe Goffredo.

👉 If you absolutely must go to Bluvet, ask specifically for referenced doctors. But for nighttime emergencies, it's best to avoid them.

Good morning:
My dog ​​Chanel underwent emergency surgery on July 22nd. I wanted to thank Dr. Felli and Dr. Alvino Vincenzo, two wonderful, professional, and extremely polite people. Thanks to their dedication and love for their work, they saved my beloved furry friend.

Thank you so much ❤️.

Luigina Dominici

After reading the comments, I admit I was a little worried, but it was too late. My cat was already hospitalized there when I read them. I should start by saying that I was in Calabria and that my partner brought her there, on the advice of our vet. She'd been vomiting since 7:00 AM, and we didn't know what to do. The team was incredibly kind from the moment my partner arrived at the clinic. They ran all the necessary tests and were extremely professional (blood tests, blood gases). The little girl also had a fever, so they gave her both something for the vomiting and an antipyretic, in addition to putting her on an IV for 24 hours. During those 24 hours, I called them often to ask about her condition, and they were always kind and answered all my questions. Even at 11:00 PM, one of the doctors answered every question, taking her temperature while we were on the phone. The next day she was discharged, even though they would have liked to keep her longer, but my partner and I couldn't bear to see her in a cage alone. They gave us the medicine to give her, explaining in detail when and how to give it. My partner also got the special kibble for gastrointestinal issues directly from them. All for a very reasonable price. That said, I don't know why there are so many negative comments because everyone was so good. Now my Ruffy is fine and we are happy. Obviously hoping we never need it, if it were to happen again, I wouldn't hesitate to take her or her little sister. Thank you all ❤️🥹

I am deeply grateful to the clinic staff who have patiently cared for my senior cat over the past few years.
A special thanks to Dr. Stefano, who accompanied me with incredible kindness and rare tact during a very difficult time.

I've been contacting them for about 5 hours about a badly injured hedgehog with two newborn kittens.
No response.

Even months ago about an injured badger, but nothing. Zero.
Italy is a country that's been gone for a long time now.
SHAME

DO NOT BRING YOUR PETS! Years ago, I brought a two-month-old kitten twice in two days. I paid €400 for two quick checkups. He wasn't dewormed, FIV-FeLV tested, or wormed, nor was he vaccinated—THEY DID NOTHING! Today, I'm coming back and asking if I can put up a pet-sitting flyer, looking at the noticeboard. A woman from the receptionist replies, grimacing, and saying, "NO!" The facts speak for themselves, as do the other terrible reviews I've found!

From the receptionist to the vet who saw my cat, everyone was very annoyed and hasty, even though I tried to be as polite as possible. I even let a woman go ahead of me who was complaining, and I didn't get a thank you from either the woman or the vet.
I had called and booked an X-ray of my paw, which the vet said was unnecessary, so they didn't do it. Instead, they sold me a €22 product made entirely of essential oils, with a half-empty bottle.
I think I'll definitely look elsewhere.

My dog ​​had food poisoning, which caused him to have seizures. I went to this clinic because it's open all night, and after they examined the dog, they wanted to give him a shot, but they weren't able to do it, so I told them to leave it alone. The vet confronted me to prevent me from leaving, saying I had to pay €90 for the visit I didn't actually get, as I came in and left immediately afterward. He wanted to call the police. After the shot, my dog ​​swells up, and for that alone, I'd kick him out of the register. They're all for profit, and they don't even care about the dog. If you have to go, ask only for Dr. Felli, he's the only one who truly loves animals.
Thanks for the review.
Terrible experience, I will never take my dog ​​to this clinic again.

260 euros for nothing, my dog ​​had a respiratory infection, which led to colitis, all of this was solved with a simple visit and a treatment that cost me 60 euros from another vet, unfortunately it was Saturday afternoon and going to the only open one, never again.

I'll start by saying I've been a client of this clinic for many years. Several years ago, Dr. Felli saved my cat, and Natasha was wonderful during the post-op period. I've only ever said good things about this clinic, and I've even referred many people.
Today was a disastrous experience. Yesterday, I called to make an appointment for my cat, specifically for a checkup and annual vaccination. I arrived and was made to wait 20 minutes longer than my scheduled appointment. I didn't worry, as emergencies happen. My turn came and they let someone else in, I complained, and they let me in. Dr. De Bonís, very perfunctory, was checking her with a stethoscope because I told him she had a scabby nose (like a cold). A minute or two into his examination, the doctor I had an appointment with, a certain Renaldo Krushova, came into the room. De Bonís dropped everything and left her with this doctor (I didn't like it at all). I repeated to the doctor that the cat needed her annual vaccination and a checkup. The doctor was hesitant because the cat needed a leg vaccination. The cat was hissing; he seemed to have little idea what to do. I suggested he call a nurse to hold my cat (she was only hissing, not getting agitated). He left, came back with De Bonís, who gave her the shot, and they put her back in the carrier; she was agitated. We locked her in, and my visit was over. They didn't take her temperature on her bottom, they didn't check her weight, they didn't check for parasites. When it came time to pay, I complained, saying they hadn't done anything and that I'd only pay for the vaccination. They told me to bring the cat back another day. Of course, I told them I wasn't playing around and I didn't go back and forth; things needed to be done right away. They charged me 45 euros for the visit and the vaccination (I still haven't figured out if they charged me for a visit that didn't happen). I noticed this on my way out, so I went back in and asked for an explanation, since I only had to pay for the vaccination. There was Dr. Renaldo Krushova, a girl in uniform whose name I don't know, and a nurse whose name I don't know. First, they made me look like a crazy person who hadn't realized they'd examined my cat, then they told me to bring her back, and then they made up the story that I'd only booked for the vaccination. Disgraceful. I'll definitely be returning to the clinic because I have a lot of respect for Dr. Felli, Natasha, and another doctor with short brown hair whose name I don't know. It's clear they love animals and know what they're doing. Dr. Krushova is a complete fail. I learned that even if the cat isn't having an emergency, I have to book with specific doctors, otherwise this is the treatment. The reception staff is unprofessional.

I brought my dachshund to the clinic because he had gradually become immobilized, causing him to leak urine, undoubtedly related to his jumping around and the resulting spinal cord compression.
Dr. Felli, thanks in part to the clinic's collaborations, managed to avoid surgery and, with the right physical therapy, stimulation, and supplements, allowed the dog to walk again, even run, and regain his bladder detrusor capacity.
I recommend anyone who works conscientiously, not looking for profit, but rather for the best interests of the dog and his family.

Dear customer, we're sorry to hear that the service was not satisfactory. We invite you to contact the clinic for further information regarding your review.

Best regards

The Clinic Staff

We went for an emergency with a 5-week-old kitten. At reception, everything was fine. When they moved us to the waiting room, one of the doctors asked us rudely if we had an appointment. He then annoyed us by telling us he didn't know how to make an appointment because both he and the other doctor were busy with other appointments. He concluded that we should make one too (even though we told him we had come for an emergency). He practically scolded us and dismissed us, even arrogantly. Let's hope it's just one bad apple...

I'm the parent of a mixed-breed dog named Asia, and I came across the Prenestina Veterinary Clinic for an emergency after being rejected by my longtime client. I immediately found courtesy and professionalism, just what we need for our furry little four-legged friends. I'm incredibly grateful to Dr. Felli and his entire team. If the need arises, I'll definitely return here for any other needs.
I highly recommend it to anyone who cares about the health of their pets.
Emiliano

Good morning, I wanted to publicly thank Dr. Adriano Felli, especially for his prompt and effective treatment of my 3-year-old German Shepherd Sheila, who had been suffering for days. THANK YOU SO MUCH.
Excellent center. Very efficient and knowledgeable doctor.

A special thanks to Dr. Adriano Felli for his efficiency, expertise, promptness, and above all, the humanity he showed my dog ​​Billy...his passionate work has allowed him to return to excellent condition and ready to face his life as best he can!!!
Clinic known by word of mouth from colleagues at work and with excellent treatment from the veterinary medical staff we cured a serious dermatitis and inflammation in a short time
Very happy with this clinic. Thank you for healing my dog.
Great service! Professional and courteous! 👏 …
Excellent service and very helpful staff, the doctors helped my dog ​​and now he is healthier than ever

Dear Dajana, thank you for sharing your positive experience with us.
Best regards
Simply fantastic, I can only recommend going there with your pets.

I brought my 7-year-old mixed-breed dog to the emergency room because he has epilepsy and was in full-blown status epilepticus. He was unconscious and had constant tonic-clonic seizures for over an hour. They rushed us in and assisted us as quickly as possible. The staff was very kind, but unfortunately lacked medical training, as they decided to solve the problem by using a continuous sedative infusion for 24 hours, rather than an antiepileptic drug as per guidelines, or generally per protocol. According to them, the clinic's protocol was to use that type of drug, which, very predictably, did nothing to stop the seizures, so my dog ​​suffered seizures for 24 hours straight. The next day, their solution was euthanasia or transfer, at my expense, to a clinic specializing in neurology. Luckily, I was financially able to do so. I can't imagine anyone in my situation who, purely out of financial constraints, would have accepted offer number one. I'll conclude by saying that at the new clinic, the MRI scan found brain lesions due to the many hours of epileptic seizures she'd suffered, thanks to them, along with significant motor deficits that persisted for over a week. All this at an even higher cost than at the specialized clinic.
I feel sorry for the vets, who were very kind but clearly unprepared.
Unfortunately, being an emergency veterinary clinic, it serves as a point of reference in emergencies, but after my experience, I wouldn't even take a goldfish there; I'd rather treat it myself.

Excellent clinic run by Dr. Adriano Felli, who treated my dog ​​with professionalism and compassion. Even on her last trip, everyone was excellent. Thanks not only to Dr. Felli, but to all the medical and administrative staff. I recommend this clinic for your dogs or cats.

If there were a zero, I'd put it at zero. We took our dog to the emergency room over a month ago because he was shaking. Everything that needed to be done was done at an exorbitant price (almost €500). He was prescribed an antibiotic for ten days. We gave him the antibiotic. No one, and I mean no one, checked on the dog afterwards. We asked to see the doctor who took care of him that night, but we couldn't get in touch. She told us to have an MRI, but the dog couldn't have one given his boldness. In fact, it was a complete failure. The MRI operator, annoyed, asked us what we were doing there with such an agitated dog. We didn't know how to answer. We did a second urine test to see if the antibiotics had worked. The urine test result was read to us absentmindedly by a foreign operator over the phone, without leaving us even a scrap of paperwork. It took almost two weeks to get it. Meanwhile, the doctor isn't answering our WhatsApp anymore. We're asking for quotes for the things our dog should have done next. We don't get any. This isn't how you treat animals.
